capabilities: Search over 150 vim commands with per-word matching across commands and descriptions
Browse commands by category such as motions, operators, text objects, visual mode, marks, and scrolling
Open the cheatsheet as a dismissable floating modal or a docked sidebar panel
Show or hide usage examples under each command in settings
Hide unused categories and assign custom hotkeys to open commands
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: Obsidian has built-in vim key bindings, but no built-in way to look up what those bindings actually are.
motivation: The author built it so users stop alt-tabbing to a browser tab every time they forget a vim motion and can keep a reference one keypress away.
problem: Obsidian has built-in vim key bindings but no built-in way to look up what those bindings are, so users leave the app to consult references.
summary: Searchable, categorized vim command reference panel that opens as a modal or sidebar inside Obsidian, alongside its built-in vim key bindings.
